data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["In epidemiology, the germ is a physical agent; in networks, the shared cause can be an abstract dependency or protocol.","Disease transmission is often biological and localized; digital dependencies are global and can activate instantaneously.","Contact tracing has a physical space to search; network dependency tracing is often a combinatorial explosion of virtual links."],"overturn_conditions":["Development of a complete, automated supply chain dependency graph that can prove the absence of shared causes.","Discovery of a statistical invariant that distinguishes latent common cause failure from independent failure."],"shared_structure":["In both, a hidden common cause links independent-looking events.","Observation of the surface variables is insufficient to identify the cause.","The cause is external to the observed system."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_002","SRC_005","SRC_006"],"transfer_claims":["Proving true independence in a decentralized network is as hard as proving a negative in epidemiology.","The appearance of uncorrelated failure is not evidence of independence; it may merely indicate the shared cause has not yet been triggered."]},"claim":"The distinction between independent and merely uncorrelated failures hinges on whether a shared latent cause exists; evidence of true independence requires proving the absence of common dependencies (e.g., cloud providers, software libraries, datasets), which is empirically intractable.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If formal verification of the entire supply chain and operational stack is possible and complete.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the network is designed with provable air-gaps or cryptographic isolation that precludes shared dependencies.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If a statistical test can distinguish the signature of latent shared causes from genuine independence.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Failures appear uncorrelated until a shared cause (e.g., an AWS outage, a shared open-source library vulnerability, or a common training dataset bias) is triggered. Because the shared cause is latent and often external to the operators' control, it is impossible to rule out through observation alone. Thus, independence is a negative claim that cannot be fully verified empirically.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
